nodes.label: YOLOv4 Prediction Showcase Figure
nodes.description: README showcase figure for the yolo-v4-tf.keras port: a matplotlib render (visible pixel axes running to ~2050 x ~1500) of inference on a crowded indoor social gathering. A dozen-plus multi-coloured boxes labelled 'person' carry scores from 0.99 down to 0.38, alongside non-person detections 'cake 0.62', 'bottle 0.9x' and 'diningtable'. Boxes overlap heavily and several people at the rear are missed or double-boxed.
nodes.rationale: Publishing a figure that includes low-confidence 0.38 boxes and visible misses, rather than a cherry-picked clean scene, documents the honest operating point of the ported weights.

nodes.label: Class-Plus-Confidence Label Annotation
nodes.description: The detector's drawing convention: every surviving box is captioned with its predicted class name and a two-decimal objectness/class score, with box colour varying per instance. The spread of printed scores (0.99, 0.94, 0.90, 0.84, 0.62, 0.57, 0.40, 0.38) makes the effective score threshold and the NMS behaviour directly auditable from the figure.
nodes.rationale: Printing the numeric score next to each box lets a reader choose a deployment threshold by eye instead of re-running inference, which is why the demo keeps sub-0.5 boxes visible.

nodes.label: COCO Pretrained Multi-Class Detection Baseline
nodes.description: Evidence that the Keras/TensorFlow re-implementation loads and correctly reproduces original Darknet COCO weights, since it emits the standard 80-class vocabulary (person, cake, bottle, diningtable) with plausible scores on an unseen photograph. It is a weight-porting correctness check, not a poultry model.
nodes.rationale: Verifying the port against stock COCO weights before any fine-tuning isolates conversion bugs from training bugs; 'bird' exists in COCO but is not fit for broilers, so domain fine-tuning is still required.
